The world's leading AI research center completed the most comprehensive study ever on kids and AI.

They surveyed 1,800+ children, parents, and teachers in UK.

Here's what they found:

(spoiler: children are outsmarting adults on AI) https://t.co/Ci6wh3RrfU

The Alan Turing Institute surveyed 780 children aged 8-12 and 1,001 teachers across UK schools.

Plus, they ran workshops where kids directly tested generative AI tools like ChatGPT and DALL-E.

The results reveal how AI is already reshaping childhood:

→ 52% of private school kids use AI vs only 18% of state school kids.

57% of private school teachers are aware of their students' use of generative AI for schoolwork, compared to 37% of state schoolteachers.

The private school AI divide is creating a new class system. https://t.co/OU5M9yMHIt

→ AI sometimes acts racist which can discourage children from using it

Children of colour often feel frustrated when AI-generated images don't represent them.

Many abandon the tools entirely after seeing outputs that erase their existence. https://t.co/zSlbhOkgG5

→ 78% of children with additional learning needs use ChatGPT vs 53% without.

They're finding ways AI helps them communicate thoughts they couldn't express before. The technology is becoming their voice.

This is awesome if you ask me. https://t.co/mXjBjQmLiO

→ Parents aren't concerned with AI cheating (41%).

The real problem here is blind trust.

76% of parents worry kids are becoming too trusting of AI without thinking critically. 72% of teachers share a similar concern. https://t.co/TIzOQWCt4H

→ When kids learned about AI's massive energy and water costs, many chose to stop using it entirely.

Gen Alpha cares more about climate impact than adults realize.

But in this case they're wrong ↓ https://t.co/1KhEBlfkCZ

A single ChatGPT query (0.3Wh) uses about the same energy as turning on an LED lightbulb for 5 minutes.

Streaming a 1hr video on Netflix consumes around 400-800Wh (significantly more than 100s of AI queries).

Stop believing pseudo-eco stuff. https://t.co/m3bCpBmRjF

→ Despite fears AI kills creativity, kids still prefer physical art materials over AI for creative tasks when given the choice.

Tactile beats digital. Human touch trumps artificial generation. Always.

A combination of both is ideal. https://t.co/o9SOnhQ3kl

→ The age-specific usage pattern shows cognitive development in action.

• 8-year-olds use AI for fun and entertainment
• 12-year-olds use it for homework help

As kids mature, AI shifts from toy to tool.
Their needs evolve with their minds. https://t.co/RQA5EOsZ9y

This data really tells us that kids aren't passive victims of AI.

They use it better than most adults.

And in this case, they are active decision-makers. They choose when to engage, when to walk away, and what values matter most.

Bottom line:

AI is already reshaping childhood whether we acknowledge it or not.

We need to give them the knowledge, access, and representation they need to use it wisely.

Their future depends on getting this right.

The world's leading AI research center completed the most comprehensive study ever on kids and AI.

They surveyed 1,800+ children, parents, and teachers in UK.

Here's what they found:

(spoiler: children are outsmarting adults on AI) https://t.co/Ci6wh3RrfU

The Alan Turing Institute surveyed 780 children aged 8-12 and 1,001 teachers across UK schools.

Plus, they ran workshops where kids directly tested generative AI tools like ChatGPT and DALL-E.

The results reveal how AI is already reshaping childhood:

→ 52% of private school kids use AI vs only 18% of state school kids.

57% of private school teachers are aware of their students' use of generative AI for schoolwork, compared to 37% of state schoolteachers.

The private school AI divide is creating a new class system. https://t.co/OU5M9yMHIt

→ AI sometimes acts racist which can discourage children from using it

Children of colour often feel frustrated when AI-generated images don't represent them.

Many abandon the tools entirely after seeing outputs that erase their existence. https://t.co/zSlbhOkgG5

→ 78% of children with additional learning needs use ChatGPT vs 53% without.

They're finding ways AI helps them communicate thoughts they couldn't express before. The technology is becoming their voice.

This is awesome if you ask me. https://t.co/mXjBjQmLiO

→ Parents aren't concerned with AI cheating (41%).

The real problem here is blind trust.

76% of parents worry kids are becoming too trusting of AI without thinking critically. 72% of teachers share a similar concern. https://t.co/TIzOQWCt4H

→ When kids learned about AI's massive energy and water costs, many chose to stop using it entirely.
